subproblems.title: Support lemma (Simon 6.2.11): a current vanishes on test forms supported away from its support (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, let S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be a current in U (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U n: a sequentially continuous linear functional on the space 𝒟ⁿ(U) of smooth n-forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U) and let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). The support of S is spt S = U ∖ Z_S, where Z_S is the union of all open W ⊆ ℝ^P with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and S(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W (Simon Ch. 6, 2.11, as formalized by GeometricCurrentOn.support). If tsupport ω ∩ spt S = ∅, then S(ω) = 0. This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dtc_vanish_off_support (node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.vanish_off_support-a1), which is reused.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted declaration dtc_vanish_off_support with byte-identical frozen Lean type; in this decomposition it is a leaf used by mass_zero_off_support, cycle and region_bound. Its audited proof follows.
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Definition 2.11 (chapter-06.txt lines 296–301) and the standard partition-of-unity argument; Simon uses this property tacitly (e.g. in 2.12). Write 𝒲 for the family of open sets W ⊆ ℝ^P with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and S vanishing on W (S(η) = 0 whenever η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and tsupport η ⊆ W); thus Z_S = ⋃𝒲 and spt S = U ∖ Z_S.
1. Since ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), ω is smooth with compact support, so C := tsupport ω is compact, and C ⊆ U. If C = ∅ then ω = 0 and S(ω) = 0 by linearity; assume C ≠ ∅.
2. From C ⊆ U and C ∩ (U ∖ Z_S) = ∅ we get C ⊆ Z_S = ⋃𝒲. The members of 𝒲 are open and C is compact, so there are W_1, …, W_N ∈ 𝒲 with C ⊆ W_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ W_N.
3. Choose a smooth partition of unity on the compact (hence closed) set C subordinate to the open cover (W_i)_{i≤N}: C^∞ functions χ_1, …, χ_N : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with tsupport χ_i ⊆ W_i for every i and Σ_{i=1}^N χ_i(x) = 1 for every x ∈ C. (Such partitions exist on the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P, e.g. Mathlib SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate with the model 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P), or directly from smooth bump functions, Mathlib exists_contDiff_tsupport_subset.)
4. For each i put ω_i := χ_i ω, i.e. ω_i(x) = χ_i(x)·ω(x). Then ω_i is smooth and tsupport ω_i ⊆ tsupport χ_i ∩ tsupport ω ⊆ W_i ∩ C. Hence tsupport ω_i is compact and contained in U, so ω_i ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); and tsupport ω_i ⊆ W_i with W_i ∈ 𝒲, so S(ω_i) = 0.
5. Σ_{i=1}^N ω_i = ω pointwise: for x ∈ C, Σ_i χ_i(x)ω(x) = ω(x); for x ∉ C, ω(x) = 0 and hence ω_i(x) = 0 for all i. By linearity of S on 𝒟ⁿ(U), S(ω) = Σ_{i=1}^N S(ω_i) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: tsupport ω is a compact subset of U missing spt S = U ∖ Z_S, so finitely many open W_i (closure compact in U) on which S vanishes cover it.
A smooth partition of unity χ_i on tsupport ω subordinate to the W_i splits ω = Σ χ_i ω, each χ_i ω a test form in U supported in W_i.
S(χ_i ω) = 0 for each i, hence S(ω) = 0 by linearity.

subproblems.title: Mass formula and support of an integer multiplicity current (Simon 6.3.2(3), 6.2.12) — reused accepted declaration
subproblems.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep: M ⊆ U Borel and countably n-rectifiable, θ : ℝ^P → ℕ measurable with θ ≥ 1 on M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, ξ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable and, Hⁿ-a.e. on M, equal to ±τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ for an orthonormal basis τ of the approximate tangent space) with T = τ(M, θ, ξ), i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Let μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M (R.measure). Then (i) M_W(T) = μ_R(W) in [0, ∞] for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, where M_W(T) is the supremum of T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; (ii) spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R. This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support (node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.imrep_mass_and_support-a1), which is reused.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W) ∧ T.support = U ∩ R.measure.support
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted declaration dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support with byte-identical frozen Lean type; in this decomposition it is a leaf used by region_bound (part (i)). Its audited proof follows.
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(3), 2.11–2.12. Notation: μ := μ_R = R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M, |α| = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} (covectorEuclideanNorm; I strictly increasing multi-indices), dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ}, ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ := ξ(x)(α).
1. Where R.orients holds at x ∈ M (Hⁿ-a.e. on M, so μ-a.e.), ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = s·α(τ₁, …, τₙ) = s·Σ_I α(e_I)det(τ^I) with τ orthonormal, s = ±1 (multilinearity, alternation; τ^I = rows I of the matrix of τ), and Σ_I det(τ^I)² = det(τᵀτ) = 1 (Cauchy–Binet). So |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| (Cauchy–Schwarz), and ξ^♭(x) := Σ_I ⟨dx^I, ξ(x)⟩dx^I has coefficients s·det(τ^I), so |ξ^♭(x)| = 1 = ⟨ξ^♭(x), ξ(x)⟩ (n = 0: I = ∅, ξ(x) = ±evaluation, ξ^♭(x) = ±1). ξ^♭ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (continuous linear in ξ; R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient).
2. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable: a.e. strongly measurable, zero off the compact spt ω ⊆ U, a.e. bounded by θ·sup|ω| (step 1), and ∫_{M∩spt ω}θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult). So T(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩dμ.
3. For open W and ω admissible for M_W(T) (ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), spt ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1), ⟨ω, ξ⟩ ≤ 1 μ-a.e. (step 1) and ω = 0 off W, so T(ω) ≤ μ(W) (step 2). So M_W(T) ≤ μ(W).
4. For real t < μ(W) (μ(W) = ∞ allowed) we find admissible ω with T(ω) > t. G := W ∩ U is open and σ-compact, μ(G) = μ(W) (M ⊆ U), and μ, finite on compacts of U, is Radon on G (Simon Ch. 1, 1.15): inner regular by compacts, outer regular on finite-measure sets. Fix η > 0 and a compact K ⊆ G with μ(K) > t + 4η. (a) Lusin (Simon 1.17): a compact K' ⊆ K with μ(K ∖ K') < η, ξ^♭|K' continuous, |ξ^♭| = 1 = ⟨ξ^♭, ξ⟩ μ-a.e. on K'. (b) An open V ⊇ K' with V̄ ⊆ G compact, μ(V ∖ K') < η. (c) Extend ξ^♭|K' coefficientwise continuously to ℝ^P (Tietze), retract radially onto the closed |·|-unit ball of Λⁿ(ℝ^P), multiply by a continuous χ: ℝ^P → [0, 1], χ = 1 on K', spt χ ⊆ V: g is continuous, spt g ⊆ V compact, |g| ≤ 1, g = ξ^♭ on K'. (d) g_ε := φ_ε ∗ g (coefficientwise, standard mollifier): for 0 < ε < dist(spt g, ℝ^P ∖ V) it is C^∞ with compact support in V ⊆ W ∩ U, |g_ε(x)| ≤ ∫φ_ε(x − y)|g(y)|dy ≤ 1 (convexity of the norm), and g_ε → g uniformly; so g_ε is admissible. (e) With δ_ε := sup|g_ε − g|·μ(V̄) → 0 (μ(V̄) < ∞), steps 2, 1 give T(g_ε) = ∫⟨g_ε, ξ⟩dμ ≥ ∫_{K'}⟨g, ξ⟩dμ − ∫_{V∖K'}|⟨g, ξ⟩|dμ − δ_ε ≥ μ(K') − η − δ_ε ≥ μ(K) − 2η − δ_ε > t + 2η − δ_ε > t for small ε. With step 3 this is (i).
5. spt T = U ∖ Z (GeometricCurrentOn.support; Simon 2.11), Z the union of the open W with W̄ ⊆ U compact and T(ω) = 0 whenever spt ω ⊆ W; x ∈ spt μ iff μ(B) > 0 for every neighbourhood B of x. (a) If x ∈ U ∩ spt μ lay in such a W, then M_W(T) = 0, so μ(W) = 0 by (i), contradicting x ∈ spt μ; so U ∩ spt μ ⊆ spt T. (b) spt T ⊆ U. If x ∈ U ∖ spt μ, take r > 0 with μ(B_r(x)) = 0, B̄_r(x) ⊆ U; by step 2 T(ω) = 0 whenever spt ω ⊆ B_r(x), so x ∈ Z, x ∉ spt T. Hence (ii).
proof_key_steps: Cauchy–Binet: |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α| μ-a.e., and ξ^♭ satisfies |ξ^♭| = 1 = ⟨ξ^♭, ξ⟩.
Integral formula T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
Upper bound: admissible ω give T(ω) ≤ μ(W), so M_W(T) ≤ μ(W).
Lower bound: Lusin, Tietze, radial retraction, cutoff and mollification of ξ^♭ give admissible forms with T(ω) > t for each real t < μ(W).
Support: by (i) and the integral formula, the zero region Z of T is U ∖ spt μ, so spt T = U ∩ spt μ.

subproblems.title: Calculus of integer multiplicity representations: locality of approximate tangent spaces, restriction, differences, orientation bound (reused accepted declaration; the parent's (IMC))
subproblems.statement: (a) Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel sets with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, M has approximate tangent space Q at x (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) if and only if M' does. (b) If U ⊆ ℝ^P is open, R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U (contract structure) and E is Borel, then (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U and it represents some current in 𝒟_n(U). (c) If U is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) are integer multiplicity (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity), then so is A − B. (d) For every IMRep R in any U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier, |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α (|·| the Euclidean coefficient norm). This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.im_calculus-a1), which is reused; its type is also byte-identical to the second conjunct of the parent's sibling foundations, cited in the parent proof as (IMC).

Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the density argument in the proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒” (chapter-03.txt lines 107–160); Ch. 6, Remarks 3.2(1) and 2.9 (chapter-06.txt lines 287–293, 755–768), stated in the book without proof; and Ch. 6, Remark 2.6 for the orientation bound. Hⁿ := μHE[n] throughout. For x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap). The statement has four parts: (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces, (b) restriction of a representation to a Borel set, (c) differences of integer multiplicity currents, (d) the orientation bound |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α|; U is open in (a)–(c).

Preliminaries.
(P0) Normalization: SimonGMT's density theorems are stated for simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n, which equals μHE[n] for natural n (SimonGMT Chapter02 simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, with simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure); hence null sets, finiteness and densities transfer verbatim, and Hⁿ is Borel regular (every set has a Borel hull of the same measure).
(P1) Scaling: for every set A, Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(A)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(A) (Mathlib Measure.hausdorffMeasure_smul₀ and invariance of Hausdorff measure under isometries). Hence for Borel A and bounded Borel f, ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} f dHⁿ = r^{−n}∫_A f(η_{x,r}(y)) dHⁿ(y).
(P2) Density zero (SimonGMT Chapter01 simon_theorem_3_6, for the Borel regular outer measure Hⁿ, cf. simon_remark_3_7_hausdorff): if D is Borel with Hⁿ(D) < ∞, then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ D, lim_{r↓0} Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x))/(ω_n rⁿ) = 0.
(P3) Cauchy–Binet. For n×P matrices A, B, det(ABᵀ) = Σ_I det(A_I) det(B_I), the sum over increasing I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n) in {1, …, P}, A_I the n×n submatrix of columns I. Proof: the j-th column of ABᵀ is Σ_k B_{jk}A_{·k}, so by multilinearity det(ABᵀ) = Σ_{k_1,…,k_n} B_{1k_1}⋯B_{nk_n} det(A_{·k_1}, …, A_{·k_n}); terms with a repeated index vanish, and grouping the remaining tuples by their underlying increasing tuple I (k = I ∘ σ for a permutation σ) gives Σ_I det(A_I) Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_j B_{j, I_{σ(j)}} = Σ_I det(A_I)det(B_I). (For n > P both sides are 0 — no increasing I, and rank ABᵀ < n.)
(P4) Orientation bound. If τ_1, …, τ_n are orthonormal in ℝ^P and ⟨α, ζ⟩ = ±α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors α, then |⟨α, ζ⟩| ≤ |α| (Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm). Proof: with A_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩, multilinearity and the alternating property give α(τ) = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_I); by Cauchy–Schwarz and (P3), |α(τ)| ≤ |α|(Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2} = |α| det(AAᵀ)^{1/2} = |α|, since AAᵀ = (⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) is the identity. For n = 0, |α(∅)| = |α|.
(P5) Two unit orientations of the same n-dimensional subspace Q differ by a sign: if τ, τ' are orthonormal bases of Q, τ'_i = Σ_j O_{ij}τ_j with O orthogonal, and α(τ') = det(O)α(τ) = ±α(τ) for every alternating α. Hence IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q and IsUnitOrientationOf ζ' Q imply ζ' = ζ or ζ' = −ζ, and IsUnitOrientationOf (−ζ) Q holds whenever IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q.
(P6) If R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in an open U, then Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (θ ≥ 1 on M).

(d) Orientation bound. By the orientation field of an IMRep, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier there is Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient x) Q, i.e. an orthonormal τ with ⟨α, R.orient x⟩ = ±α(τ) for all α; by (P4), |R.orient x α| ≤ |α| for all α. (No openness of U is needed.)

(a) Locality. Let U be open, M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and D := M' ∖ M.
1. For R ∈ ℕ let U_R := {x ∈ U : |x| < R, infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/R} (U_R := {|x| < R} if U = ℝ^P). U_R is open, closure(U_R) is a compact subset of U, and U_R ↑ U. D_R := D ∩ U_R is Borel with Hⁿ(D_R) ≤ Hⁿ(M' ∩ closure(U_R)) < ∞. By (P2) there is an Hⁿ-null set Z_R such that every x ∉ D_R ∪ Z_R satisfies Hⁿ(D_R ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ) as r ↓ 0. Let Z := ⋃_R Z_R, and let Z' ⊇ Z be a Borel Hⁿ-null set (P0). Let x ∈ M ∖ Z'; choose R with x ∈ U_R and r₀ > 0 with B̄_{r₀}(x) ⊆ U_R. Then x ∉ D_R (as x ∈ M) and D ∩ B̄_r(x) = D_R ∩ B̄_r(x) for r < r₀, so Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ).
2. Fix such x, a subspace Q and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_ρ(0). For r < r₀/ρ the sets η_{x,r}(M), η_{x,r}(M') meet B_ρ(0) in sets of finite Hⁿ-measure, so the integrals below are genuine Bochner integrals. Since η_{x,r} is injective, η_{x,r}(M') is the disjoint union of η_{x,r}(M) and η_{x,r}(D), and by (P1)
 |∫_{η_{x,r}(M')} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ| = |∫_{η_{x,r}(D)} f dHⁿ| ≤ |f|_∞ r^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ B_{rρ}(x)) → 0 as r ↓ 0.
Hence for every f the two families of integrals have the same limit as r → 0⁺ or both have none; the condition finrank Q = n is common to both predicates. So HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q for every x ∈ M ∖ Z' and every Q; the exceptional set M ∩ Z' is null for Hⁿ⌞M. ∎

(b) Restriction. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in the open set U and E a Borel set. Define R' with carrier M ∩ E and the same mult θ and orient ξ.
1. Structure fields: M ∩ E is Borel and contained in U; countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono); θ is measurable and θ > 0 on M ∩ E; ∫_{M∩E∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U; ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E) ≤ Hⁿ⌞M.
2. Orientation: by (P6) and (a) applied to M ∩ E ⊆ M ⊆ U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ E and all Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ E) x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. With the orientation field of R (Hⁿ-a.e. on M) this gives the orientation field of R'.
3. The current: A(ω) := ∫_{M∩E} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). By (d), |θ⟨ω, ξ⟩| ≤ |ω|_∞ θ 1_{tsupport ω} Hⁿ-a.e. on M, and tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, so the integrand is integrable; A is linear. If ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges: supports in a fixed compact K ⊆ U and uniform convergence of all derivatives, in particular |ω_j|_∞ → 0 since all norms on the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors are equivalent), then |A(ω_j)| ≤ |ω_j|_∞ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ → 0. So A is a GeometricCurrentOn U n and R' represents A (IMRep.Represents, IMRep.action). ∎

(c) Differences. Let A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, be represented by R_A = (M_A, θ_A, ξ_A) and R_B = (M_B, θ_B, ξ_B).
1. (Borel versions and good points.) Choose Borel ξ̃_A, ξ̃_B equal to ξ_A, ξ_B Hⁿ-a.e. on M_A, resp. M_B (a.e. strong measurability; set them 0 off the carriers). Let G be the set of x ∈ M_A ∪ M_B such that: if x ∈ M_A, then ξ̃_A(x) = ξ_A(x) and there is Q_A(x) with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M_A x Q_A(x) and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_A x) Q_A(x); the analogous condition for B if x ∈ M_B; and, for each pair (N, N') among (M_A ∩ M_B, M_A), (M_A ∩ M_B, M_B) with x ∈ N, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N' x Q for every Q. By the orientation fields of R_A, R_B, by (P6) and by (a), (M_A ∪ M_B) ∖ G is Hⁿ-null; let N₀ ⊇ (M_A ∪ M_B) ∖ G be a Borel Hⁿ-null set (P0).
2. (Overlap.) Let x ∈ (M_A ∩ M_B) ∖ N₀. The approximate tangent space of M_A ∩ M_B at x exists and equals Q_A(x) and also Q_B(x) (the equivalences defining G and uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces, SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique); so Q_A(x) = Q_B(x) and by (P5) ξ̃_B(x) = ε(x)ξ̃_A(x) with ε(x) ∈ {1, −1}. Put ε(x) := 1 if ξ̃_B(x) = ξ̃_A(x) and ε(x) := −1 otherwise (a Borel function).
3. (Data.) Put O := (M_A ∩ M_B) ∖ N₀, k := θ_A − εθ_B ∈ ℤ on O, and
 M := ((M_A ∖ M_B) ∪ (M_B ∖ M_A) ∪ {x ∈ O : k(x) ≠ 0}) ∖ N₀,
 θ := θ_A on M_A ∖ M_B, θ_B on M_B ∖ M_A, |k| on O, 0 elsewhere (Borel, ℕ-valued),
 ζ := ξ̃_A on M_A ∖ M_B, −ξ̃_B on M_B ∖ M_A, sign(k)ξ̃_A on O, 0 elsewhere (Borel).
For every x ∉ N₀: θ(x)1_M(x)ζ(x) = θ_A(x)1_{M_A}(x)ξ̃_A(x) − θ_B(x)1_{M_B}(x)ξ̃_B(x) (on O with k = 0 both sides vanish; on O with k ≠ 0, θ_Aξ̃_A − θ_Bεξ̃_A = kξ̃_A = |k| sign(k)ξ̃_A; the other cases are immediate).
4. (Representation.) For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), integrating ⟨ω, ·⟩ against both sides of step 3 (N₀ is null; all integrands are integrable by (d), since θ1_M ≤ θ_A1_{M_A} + θ_B1_{M_B}):
 ∫_M θ⟨ω, ζ⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_{M_A} θ_A⟨ω, ξ_A⟩ dHⁿ − ∫_{M_B} θ_B⟨ω, ξ_B⟩ dHⁿ = A(ω) − B(ω) = (A − B)(ω).
5. (Structure fields.) M is Borel, M ⊆ M_A ∪ M_B ⊆ U, and M is countably n-rectifiable (countablyRectifiable_iUnion, CountablyRectifiable.mono). θ is Borel and ℕ-valued with θ ≥ 1 on M (|k| ≥ 1 where k ≠ 0), and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M_A∩K} θ_A dHⁿ + ∫_{M_B∩K} θ_B dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U. ζ is Borel, hence a.e. strongly measurable.
6. (Orientation.) For compact K ⊆ U, Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(M_A ∩ K) + Hⁿ(M_B ∩ K) < ∞ by (P6) applied to R_A, R_B. Apply (a) to the pairs (M ∩ M_A ⊆ M_A), (M ∩ M_A ⊆ M), (M ∩ M_B ⊆ M_B), (M ∩ M_B ⊆ M) (all Borel, contained in U, with locally finite Hⁿ-measure): for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ M_A the approximate tangent spaces of M and of M_A at x coincide (both equal that of M ∩ M_A), and similarly for M_B. Let x be such a point, x ∉ N₀. If x ∈ M_A, then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_A(x) and ζ(x) = ±ξ_A(x) (cases M_A ∖ M_B and O, using ξ̃_A(x) = ξ_A(x)), a unit orientation of Q_A(x) by (P5). If x ∈ M_B ∖ M_A, ζ(x) = −ξ_B(x) is a unit orientation of Q_B(x), the approximate tangent space of M at x. Hence the orientation field holds Hⁿ-a.e. on M.
So (M, θ, ζ) is an IMRep in U representing A − B, and A − B is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: (d): Cauchy–Binet gives Σ_I det(A_I)² = det(AAᵀ) = 1 for orthonormal τ, so |α(τ)| ≤ |α|.
(a): the density of Hⁿ⌞(M′∖M) vanishes at Hⁿ-a.e. point of M (SimonGMT simon_theorem_3_6 on an exhaustion of U), so the blow-up integrals of M and M′ have the same limits.
(b): all IMRep fields restrict; the orientation field transfers by (a); continuity of the restricted current from local integrability and (d).
(c): on the overlap the approximate tangent spaces agree a.e., so the orientations differ by a sign; combine multiplicities θ_A ∓ θ_B, drop cancellation points, and verify the IMRep fields with (a).

subproblems.title: Restriction of an integer multiplicity current to an open subdomain is integer multiplicity (reused accepted declaration; the parent's (F5))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and V ⊆ U ⊆ ℝ^P with V open. Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be integer multiplicity, i.e. T = τ(M, θ, ξ) for some IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) of U (Simon 6.3.1). Then the restriction T⌞V ∈ 𝒟_n(V) is integer multiplicity in V. Here T⌞V = T.restrictDomain, T⌞V(ω) = T(ιω) with ι = testFormOnInclusion. Explicitly, T⌞V is represented by (M ∩ V, θ, ξ). This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dtc_restrictDomain_isIntegerMultiplicity (node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.localize-a1.restrict_im-a1), which is reused.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U V : Set (Euclid P)) (hVU : V ⊆ U) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen V → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → IsIntegerMultiplicity (T.restrictDomain hVU)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted declaration dtc_restrictDomain_isIntegerMultiplicity with byte-identical frozen Lean type; in this decomposition it is a leaf used by add_restrict. Its audited proof follows.
Source: (F5) of the parent proof (the domain restriction X|_V of an integer multiplicity current is integer multiplicity, represented by the restricted triple), Simon Ch. 6, 3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–753) and Ch. 3, 1.4. Reused accepted declaration dtc_restrictDomain_isIntegerMultiplicity; the proof below is its audited proof, except that the citation of a lemma of its original branch in step 7 is replaced by the elementary locality of approximate tangent spaces at points of the open set V.
Let R = (M, θ, ξ) = (R.carrier, R.mult, R.orient) be an IMRep of U with R.Represents T. Define R′ with carrier M ∩ V, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ. We check the fields of IMRep V n, then the representation.
1. Measurability: M is Borel and V is open, so M ∩ V is Borel.
2. M ∩ V ⊆ V.
3. Rectifiability: M ∩ V ⊆ M, and M is countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono).
4. θ is measurable, and θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M ∩ V ⊆ M.
5. Local integrability in V. Let K be compact with K ⊆ V. Then (M ∩ V) ∩ K = M ∩ K because K ⊆ V. Also K ⊆ V ⊆ U, so ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by the local integrability of R in U.
6. ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ V), because Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ V) ≤ Hⁿ⌞M (Measure.restrict_mono; AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure).
7. Orientation. By the field orients of R, for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. A property holding Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. also holds Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ V)-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset), and Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ V)-a.e. x lies in M ∩ V (ae_restrict_mem). Fix such an x ∈ M ∩ V and its Q; we show HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ V) x Q. The condition finrank Q = n is common to both predicates. Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P); choose ρ > 0 with f = 0 outside B_ρ(0) and δ > 0 with B_δ(x) ⊆ V (V is open). For r > 0 let η_r(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap x r), a homeomorphism of ℝ^P, so that η_r(M) and η_r(M ∩ V) are Borel and η_r(M ∩ V) ⊆ η_r(M). For 0 < r < δ/ρ: if y ∈ M and η_r(y) ∈ B_ρ(0), then |y − x| < rρ < δ, so y ∈ V; hence η_r(M) ∖ η_r(M ∩ V) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ B_ρ(0), where f = 0, and therefore ∫_{η_r(M)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{η_r(M∩V)} f dHⁿ (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_diff_eq_zero). The two functions of r agree on (0, δ/ρ), a set belonging to the filter 𝓝[>] 0, so they have the same limit ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r → 0⁺. As f was arbitrary, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ V) x Q holds, and the same Q still satisfies IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. Hence R′ is an IMRep of V.
8. Representation. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V). The form ιω (testFormOnInclusion) has the same underlying form, so (T⌞V)(ω) = T(ιω) = R.action ω = ∫_M θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x). For x ∈ M ∖ (M ∩ V) we have x ∉ V ⊇ tsupport ω, so ω(x) = 0 and the integrand θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) vanishes (ξ(x) is linear). M is measurable and M ∩ V ⊆ M, so ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_{M∩V} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_diff_eq_zero), and the right side is R′.action ω. Thus R′ represents T⌞V, and T⌞V is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: Restrict a representation (M, θ, ξ) of T to (M ∩ V, θ, ξ): measurability, rectifiability, positivity and local integrability on compact subsets of V ⊆ U are inherited.
At x ∈ V, for r < δ/ρ the blow-ups η_r(M) and η_r(M ∩ V) coincide on B_ρ(0) ⊇ spt f, so M and M ∩ V have the same approximate tangent space at x; the orientation field transfers.
Forms supported in V vanish on M ∖ V, so the integral over M equals the integral over M ∩ V.

Suppose μ(G) ≤ ν(G) + c for every open G ⊇ E such that closure(G) is compact and contained in U. Then μ(E) ≤ ν(E) + c. This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration lcmp_measure_le_add_of_open_nhds (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.local_comparison-a1.compact_outer_bound-a1), which is reused.

Source: (F3) of the parent proof (from open sets to other Borel sets by outer regularity of the finite restricted measures), needed for the compact sets Σ_α = {ψ_c = α} (step 8(c)) and the sphere ∂B_G (step 7(e)). It passes an inequality between measures from open neighbourhoods of a compact set to the set itself by continuity from above. Reused accepted declaration lcmp_measure_le_add_of_open_nhds; its audited proof follows.

1. If E = ∅ then μ(E) = 0 and there is nothing to prove; the argument below also covers this case. Choose δ > 0 with C_δ := {x : dist(x, E) ≤ δ} ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). For k ∈ ℕ put r_k := δ/(k + 2) ∈ (0, δ) and G_k := {x : dist(x, E) < r_k} (open thickening).
2. Each G_k is open and contains E (r_k > 0). closure(G_k) ⊆ {dist(·, E) ≤ r_k} ⊆ C_δ ⊆ U, and C_δ is compact (closed thickening of a compact set in the proper space ℝ^P), so closure(G_k) is compact and contained in U. By hypothesis and monotonicity, μ(E) ≤ μ(G_k) ≤ ν(G_k) + c for every k.
3. Since r_k decreases, (G_k) is decreasing. ⋂_k G_k = E: E ⊆ G_k for all k; conversely, if dist(x, E) < r_k for all k, then for every ε > 0 some r_k < ε gives x ∈ {dist(·, E) < ε}, so x ∈ ⋂_{ε>0} {dist(·, E) < ε} = closure(E) (Metric.closure_eq_iInter_thickening) = E, E being compact and hence closed. The G_k are open, hence measurable, and ν(G_0) ≤ ν(C_δ) < ∞.
4. By continuity from above (Mathlib tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop), ν(G_k) → ν(E). Addition of the constant c is continuous on [0, ∞], so ν(G_k) + c → ν(E) + c, and letting k → ∞ in μ(E) ≤ ν(G_k) + c gives μ(E) ≤ ν(E) + c. ∎

Each G_k is open, contains E and has compact closure in U, so μ(E) ≤ μ(G_k) ≤ ν(G_k) + c.
G_k decreases to closure(E) = E and ν(G_0) < ∞; continuity from above gives ν(G_k) → ν(E), hence μ(E) ≤ ν(E) + c.

subproblems.title: A current vanishing on forms supported away from a compact set has compact support inside it
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, K ⊆ U compact, and F ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) whose topological support is disjoint from K. Then spt F ⊆ K and spt F is compact. Here spt F = U ∖ Z(F) (GeometricCurrentOn.support), Z(F) being the union of all open W with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.

Reused comparator-accepted declaration rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish with byte-identical frozen Lean type; in this decomposition it is a leaf used by cycle (the parent proof's preliminary (p2)). Its audited proof follows.
Source: parent proof, step 6(f) (“For y ∈ U ∖ K choose s > 0 with B̄_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K … S − T vanishes on all forms supported in B_{s/2}(y), whose closure is compact and contained in U, so y ∉ spt(S − T). Thus spt(S − T) ⊆ K. Being relatively closed in U and contained in the compact K ⊆ U, spt(S − T) is compact”), isolated for an arbitrary current F; the parent applies it to F = S − T.

1. Points of U ∖ K are not in spt F. Let y ∈ U ∖ K. Since U is open and K is closed (compact), U ∖ K is open (IsOpen.sdiff), so there is s > 0 with B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K. Put W := B_{s/2}(y).
 (a) W is open and y ∈ W.
 (b) closure(W) ⊆ B̄_{s/2}(y) ⊆ B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K ⊆ U.
 (c) closure(W) is compact, as a closed subset of the compact closed ball B̄_{s/2}(y) (ℝ^P is proper).
 (d) If ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) and tsupport ω ⊆ W, then tsupport ω ⊆ B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K is disjoint from K, so F(ω) = 0.
 By (a)-(d), W is one of the sets whose union is Z(F), so y ∈ Z(F) and y ∉ spt F.

2. spt F ⊆ K. By definition spt F ⊆ U, and by step 1 no point of U ∖ K lies in spt F.

3. Compactness. From spt F = U ∖ Z(F), spt F ⊆ K and K ⊆ U, we get spt F = K ∖ Z(F). Z(F) is open, as a union of open sets (isOpen_zeroRegion). So K ∖ Z(F) is a closed subset of the compact set K, hence compact (IsCompact.diff). ∎
proof_key_steps: For y ∈ U ∖ K, a ball B_{s/2}(y) with closure in U ∖ K is a relatively compact zero set of F, so y ∉ spt F.
Hence spt F ⊆ K, and spt F = K ∖ Z(F) is compact because Z(F) is open.

subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, V ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets and let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be a current in U (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U n). Suppose V ∩ spt T = ∅, where spt T = GeometricCurrentOn.support T is U minus the union of the open sets W with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and T(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W. Then M_V(T) = 0. Here M_V(T) = T.massOn V is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ofReal(T(ω)) over the forms ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ V and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 1 (case A ∩ B_{2G} = ∅, parent case (E): “If ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ F ⊆ B_G ⊆ B_{2G}, then tsupport ω ∩ spt T = ∅, so T(ω) = 0 by (VO). By (p1), M_W(T) = 0”) together with its preliminary (p1). Here it is stated for an arbitrary current T and set V. Sibling used: (VO) vanish_off_support.
Notation: ω is admissible for M_V(T) if ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω ⊆ V and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x (massAdmissibleOn U n V). M_V(T) is the supremum in [0, ∞] of the set {ofReal(T(ω)) : ω admissible for M_V(T)}.
1. Let ω be admissible for M_V(T). Since tsupport ω ⊆ V and V ∩ spt T = ∅, also tsupport ω ∩ spt T = ∅ (Disjoint.mono_left).
2. By (VO), applied to the current T in U and the test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), T(ω) = 0. Hence ofReal(T(ω)) = ofReal(0) = 0.
3. Every element of the set whose supremum is M_V(T) is therefore 0, so M_V(T) ≤ 0 (sSup_le). In [0, ∞] the inequality M_V(T) ≤ 0 means M_V(T) = 0 (nonpos_iff_eq_zero). ∎
proof_key_steps: An admissible ω for M_V(T) has tsupport ω ⊆ V, which misses spt T, so T(ω) = 0 by vanish_off_support.
Every term ofReal(T(ω)) of the supremum defining M_V(T) is 0, hence M_V(T) = 0.

subproblems.title: The comparison cycle Y = (S − C) + Ŷ (parent step 2; Simon 7.2.4 with Remark 7.2.5(2))
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let F ⊆ ℝ^P be compact and let C, S, Ŷ ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ (m + 1)). Assume that C and S are integer multiplicity (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity), ∂S = ∂C (S.boundary = C.boundary), spt(S − C) ⊆ F, Ŷ is integer multiplicity, ∂Ŷ = 0 and spt Ŷ ⊆ F. Then some Y ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) is integer multiplicity, has ∂Y = 0, has compact support spt Y ⊆ F, and satisfies Y(ω) = (S − C)(ω) + Ŷ(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P). Here S − C is the contract's difference of currents, (S − C)(ω) = S(ω) − C(ω), and spt is GeometricCurrentOn.support.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (F : Set (Euclid P)) (C S Ŷ : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), IsCompact F → IsIntegerMultiplicity C → IsIntegerMultiplicity S → S.boundary = C.boundary → (S - C).support ⊆ F → IsIntegerMultiplicity Ŷ → Ŷ.boundary = 0 → Ŷ.support ⊆ F → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), IsIntegerMultiplicity Y ∧ Y.boundary = 0 ∧ IsCompact Y.support ∧ Y.support ⊆ F ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), Y ω = (S - C) ω + Ŷ ω
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 2 (“X := S − C is integer multiplicity ((IMC)(c)), ∂X = ∂S − ∂C = 0 (p6) and spt X ⊆ W. Y := X − (0 − Ŷ) (= X + Ŷ) is integer multiplicity (p3) and ∂Y = ∂X + ∂Ŷ = 0 (p6). If tsupport ω ∩ F = ∅, then X(ω) = 0 and Ŷ(ω) = 0 by (VO) …, so Y(ω) = 0; by (p2) spt Y ⊆ F, so spt Y is compact”). Three changes: the parent's spt(S − C) ⊆ W ⊆ F is used only as spt(S − C) ⊆ F; (p3) is realized with 0 = Ŷ − Ŷ; and (p2) is supplied by support_of_vanishing. Siblings used: (VO) vanish_off_support; (IMC) im_calculus, part (c): if A, B ∈ 𝒟_k(V) are integer multiplicity and V is open, then so is A − B; (SV) support_of_vanishing.
Conventions: all currents live in the open set ℝ^P (= univ). For currents A, B, (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) − B(ω), and 0 is the zero current. For A ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) and η ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P), ∂A(η) = A(dη), where dη ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P) is the exterior derivative of η (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, exteriorDerivativeTestOn).
1. (Integer multiplicity.) Apply (IMC)(c) in the open set ℝ^P four times. X := S − C is integer multiplicity, because C and S are. D := Ŷ − Ŷ is integer multiplicity. N := D − Ŷ is integer multiplicity. Finally Y := X − N is integer multiplicity.
2. (Values.) For every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P), Y(ω) = X(ω) − ((Ŷ(ω) − Ŷ(ω)) − Ŷ(ω)) = X(ω) + Ŷ(ω) = (S − C)(ω) + Ŷ(ω).
3. (Boundary.) Let η ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) and ζ := dη. Evaluating ∂S = ∂C at η gives S(ζ) = C(ζ), and evaluating ∂Ŷ = 0 at η gives Ŷ(ζ) = 0. Hence ∂Y(η) = Y(ζ) = (S(ζ) − C(ζ)) − ((Ŷ(ζ) − Ŷ(ζ)) − Ŷ(ζ)) = 0 − (0 − 0) = 0 = 0(η). Since η is arbitrary, ∂Y = 0 by extensionality of currents (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
4. (Vanishing away from F.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ∩ F = ∅. Since spt X = spt(S − C) ⊆ F and spt Ŷ ⊆ F, tsupport ω is disjoint from spt X and from spt Ŷ. So (VO) gives X(ω) = 0 and Ŷ(ω) = 0, and step 2 gives Y(ω) = 0.
5. (Support.) Apply (SV) with the open set ℝ^P, the compact set K := F ⊆ ℝ^P and the current Y; step 4 is its hypothesis. It gives spt Y ⊆ F, and spt Y is compact.
6. By steps 1–5, Y has all the required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: Y := (S − C) − ((Ŷ − Ŷ) − Ŷ) is integer multiplicity by im_calculus (c), and Y(ω) = (S − C)(ω) + Ŷ(ω).
∂Y(η) = S(dη) − C(dη) + Ŷ(dη) = 0, because ∂S = ∂C and ∂Ŷ = 0.
Y vanishes on forms supported away from F (vanish_off_support), so support_of_vanishing gives spt Y ⊆ F with spt Y compact.

subproblems.title: An integer multiplicity current in U plus the restriction of one in ℝ^P (parent step 3, construction of Z)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be integer multiplicity and let Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) be integer multiplicity. Then there is an integer multiplicity Z ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with Z(ω) = T(ω) + Y(ιω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Here ιω = testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) n ω is ω regarded as a test form in ℝ^P (same underlying form).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → IsIntegerMultiplicity Y → ∃ Z : GeometricCurrentOn U n, IsIntegerMultiplicity Z ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Z ω = T ω + Y (testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) n ω)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 3, first sentence (“Y|_U is integer multiplicity by (RO), so Z := T − (0 − Y|_U) ∈ 𝒟_n(U) is integer multiplicity (p3), and Z(ω) = T(ω) + Y(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U)”). Here T and Y are arbitrary integer multiplicity currents, and (p3) is realized with 0 = T − T. Siblings used: (RO) restrict_open_im; (IMC) im_calculus, part (c): differences of integer multiplicity currents in an open set are integer multiplicity.
1. Let Y|_U := Y.restrictDomain (subset_univ U) ∈ 𝒟_n(U). By definition (restrictDomain_apply), Y|_U(ω) = Y(ιω) for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). U ⊆ ℝ^P is open and Y is integer multiplicity in ℝ^P, so Y|_U is integer multiplicity in U by (RO), applied to the domains U ⊆ ℝ^P.
2. Apply (IMC)(c) in the open set U three times. T − T is integer multiplicity, because T is. Then (T − T) − Y|_U is integer multiplicity. Finally Z := T − ((T − T) − Y|_U) is integer multiplicity.
3. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), the definition of the difference of currents gives Z(ω) = T(ω) − ((T(ω) − T(ω)) − Y|_U(ω)) = T(ω) + Y|_U(ω) = T(ω) + Y(ιω). ∎
proof_key_steps: Y|_U = Y.restrictDomain (subset_univ U) is integer multiplicity in the open set U by restrict_open_im.
Z := T − ((T − T) − Y|_U) is integer multiplicity by three applications of im_calculus (c), and Z(ω) = T(ω) + Y(ιω).

subproblems.title: Three-region mass estimate for the comparison current (parent steps 4–7; Simon 7.2.4 (8)–(11))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, W, F, B ⊆ ℝ^P, T, Z ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and C, S, Ŷ, Sr, Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n). Let R be an integer multiplicity representation of T in U (IMRep U n with R.Represents T), μ_T := R.measure, and let e ∈ [0, ∞]. Assume: Z is integer multiplicity; B is open and B ⊆ U; W is open, F is compact and W ⊆ F ⊆ B; μ_T(F ∖ W) = 0; spt(S − C) ⊆ W; Ŷ is integer multiplicity with spt Ŷ ⊆ F; μ_{R′}(F ∖ W) ≤ e for every integer multiplicity representation R′ of Ŷ in ℝ^P (IMRep univ n); M(Sr) ≤ e; C(ω) = currentEval(T, ω) + Ŷ(ω) + Sr(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W; Y(ω) = (S − C)(ω) + Ŷ(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P); and Z(ω) = T(ω) + Y(ιω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), where ιω = testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) n ω. Then there is b ∈ [0, ∞] with M_B(T) = M_W(T) + b and M_B(Z) ≤ M_W(S) + e + e + b. Here M_G(A) = A.massOn G is the local mass in [0, ∞] (supremum of ofReal(A(ω)) over test forms ω of the domain of A with tsupport ω ⊆ G and Euclidean coefficient norm ≤ 1); M(Sr) = Sr.mass = M_{ℝ^P}(Sr); currentEval(T, ω) (contract currentEval) is T(ω) if ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ U, and 0 otherwise; spt is GeometricCurrentOn.support and (S − C)(ω) = S(ω) − C(ω).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W F B : Set (Euclid P)) (T Z : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n) (C S Ŷ Sr Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (e : ℝ≥0∞), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → IsIntegerMultiplicity Z → IsOpen B → B ⊆ U → IsOpen W → IsCompact F → W ⊆ F → F ⊆ B → R.measure (F \ W) = 0 → (S - C).support ⊆ W → IsIntegerMultiplicity Ŷ → Ŷ.support ⊆ F → (∀ R' : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, R'.Represents Ŷ → R'.measure (F \ W) ≤ e) → Sr.mass ≤ e → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ W → C ω = currentEval T (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) + Ŷ ω + Sr ω) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, Y ω = (S - C) ω + Ŷ ω) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Z ω = T ω + Y (testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) n ω)) → ∃ b : ℝ≥0∞, T.massOn B = T.massOn W + b ∧ Z.massOn B ≤ S.massOn W + e + e + b
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 4–7 (parent 8(b)–(d); Simon 7.2.4 (8)–(11), chapter-07.txt lines 223–260, with the modification of Remark 7.2.5(2), lines 166–175). An arbitrary open B replaces B_G, and Y, Z are given through their defining identities. Siblings used: (VO) vanish_off_support; (MR) mass_and_support, part (i): if R′ represents a current A in an open domain, then M_G(A) = μ_{R′}(G) for every open G; (COB) compact_outer_bound.
The argument is self-contained apart from these three siblings. The needed triangle inequalities for local masses are proved inline by supremum arguments. On Σ = F ∖ W, (COB) is applied in the open set U′ := U ∖ spt(S − C), so no representation of S − C is needed.
Notation. μ_T := R.measure; X := S − C; Σ := F ∖ W; O′ := B ∖ F. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), ω′ := ιω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) has the same underlying form as ω (testFormOnInclusion_coe), hence the same tsupport and the same pointwise norms. A test form ω of the domain of a current A is admissible for M_G(A) if tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, where |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm. M_G(A) is the supremum of ofReal(A(ω)) over admissible ω. So ofReal(A(ω)) ≤ M_G(A) for admissible ω (le_massOn), and M_G(A) ≤ c follows once ofReal(A(ω)) ≤ c for every admissible ω (sSup_le). By the definition of mass, M(Sr) = M_{ℝ^P}(Sr).
0. Preliminaries.
 (a) Z and Ŷ are integer multiplicity: choose an IMRep R_Z of Z in U and an IMRep R_Ŷ of Ŷ in ℝ^P. (MR)(i) in the open sets U and ℝ^P gives, for every open G ⊆ ℝ^P: M_G(T) = μ_T(G), M_G(Z) = μ_{R_Z}(G) and M_G(Ŷ) = μ_{R_Ŷ}(G).
 (b) F is compact, hence closed and Borel; W and B are open. So Σ = F ∖ W and O′ = B ∖ F are Borel and O′ is open. Σ = F ∩ (ℝ^P ∖ W) is compact, being a closed subset of the compact F.
 (c) Every measure μ on ℝ^P satisfies μ(B) = μ(W) + μ(Σ) + μ(O′). Indeed F = W ∪ Σ (W ⊆ F) and B = F ∪ O′ (F ⊆ B) are disjoint unions of Borel sets, so μ(F) = μ(W) + μ(Σ) and μ(B) = μ(F) + μ(O′).
 (d) If R′ = (M′, θ′, ξ′) is an IMRep in a set V and K ⊆ V is compact, then μ_{R′}(K) < ∞. Indeed K is Borel, so μ_{R′}(K) = ∫_K θ′ d(Hⁿ⌞M′) = ∫_{M′∩K} θ′ dHⁿ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict), which is finite by the IMRep field locallyIntegrable_mult.
 (e) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). If tsupport ω ∩ W = ∅, then X(ω′) = 0, by (VO) and spt X ⊆ W. If tsupport ω ∩ F = ∅, then also Ŷ(ω′) = 0, by (VO) and spt Ŷ ⊆ F.
1. (The T side.) Put b := μ_T(O′). By 0(a) for the open sets B and W, and 0(c) for μ_T: M_B(T) = μ_T(B) = μ_T(W) + μ_T(Σ) + μ_T(O′) = M_W(T) + 0 + b = M_W(T) + b, since μ_T(Σ) = μ_T(F ∖ W) = 0.
2. (Region O′; parent 8(b).) Let ω be admissible for M_{O′}(Z). tsupport ω ⊆ O′ misses F, hence also W ⊆ F, so X(ω′) = 0 and Ŷ(ω′) = 0 by 0(e). Thus Y(ω′) = 0 and Z(ω) = T(ω). Since ω is admissible for M_{O′}(T), ofReal(Z(ω)) = ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ M_{O′}(T). Hence M_{O′}(Z) ≤ M_{O′}(T), i.e. μ_{R_Z}(O′) ≤ μ_T(O′) = b by 0(a) (O′ is open).
3. (Region W; parent 8(d).) Let ω be admissible for M_W(Z). Then ω′ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) and tsupport ω′ = tsupport ω ⊆ W, so by hypothesis C(ω′) = currentEval(T, ω′) + Ŷ(ω′) + Sr(ω′). The underlying form of ω′ is that of ω, a test form with tsupport in U. So the first branch of the definition of currentEval applies, the test form of 𝒟ⁿ(U) built there is ω itself, and currentEval(T, ω′) = T(ω). Hence Z(ω) = T(ω) + Y(ω′) = T(ω) + S(ω′) − C(ω′) + Ŷ(ω′) = S(ω′) − Sr(ω′). Now ω′ is admissible for M_W(S) in ℝ^P (same tsupport and norms). Also −ω′ is admissible for M_{ℝ^P}(Sr) (tsupport ⊆ ℝ^P, and |−α| = |α| by covectorEuclideanNorm_neg), and Sr(−ω′) = −Sr(ω′) by linearity. Therefore ofReal(Z(ω)) = ofReal(S(ω′) + Sr(−ω′)) ≤ ofReal(S(ω′)) + ofReal(Sr(−ω′)) ≤ M_W(S) + M_{ℝ^P}(Sr) = M_W(S) + M(Sr) ≤ M_W(S) + e (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le). Hence M_W(Z) ≤ M_W(S) + e, and μ_{R_Z}(W) = M_W(Z) ≤ M_W(S) + e by 0(a) (W is open).
4. (Region Σ; parent 8(c).) spt X = ℝ^P ∖ 𝒵(X), where the zero region 𝒵(X) (GeometricCurrentOn.zeroRegion) is open (isOpen_zeroRegion); so spt X is closed and U′ := U ∩ (ℝ^P ∖ spt X) is open. Σ ⊆ U′, because Σ ⊆ F ⊆ B ⊆ U and a point of Σ ∩ spt X would lie in (F ∖ W) ∩ W = ∅. Let ν := μ_T + μ_{R_Ŷ}. For compact K ⊆ U′, ν(K) = μ_T(K) + μ_{R_Ŷ}(K) < ∞ by 0(d), using K ⊆ U for R and K ⊆ ℝ^P for R_Ŷ. Now let G′ be open with Σ ⊆ G′, closure(G′) compact and closure(G′) ⊆ U′; then G′ ⊆ U′. Let ω be admissible for M_{G′}(Z). Then tsupport ω ⊆ G′ misses spt X, so X(ω′) = 0 by (VO) and Z(ω) = T(ω) + Ŷ(ω′). Since ω is admissible for M_{G′}(T) and ω′ for M_{G′}(Ŷ), ofReal(Z(ω)) ≤ ofReal(T(ω)) + ofReal(Ŷ(ω′)) ≤ M_{G′}(T) + M_{G′}(Ŷ). Hence M_{G′}(Z) ≤ M_{G′}(T) + M_{G′}(Ŷ), i.e. μ_{R_Z}(G′) ≤ μ_T(G′) + μ_{R_Ŷ}(G′) = ν(G′) + 0 by 0(a) (G′ is open). Apply (COB) with the open set U′, the compact set E := Σ ⊆ U′, μ := μ_{R_Z}, ν and c := 0. It gives μ_{R_Z}(Σ) ≤ ν(Σ) + 0 = μ_T(F ∖ W) + μ_{R_Ŷ}(F ∖ W) = 0 + μ_{R_Ŷ}(F ∖ W) ≤ e, the last step by the hypothesis on representations of Ŷ applied to R′ := R_Ŷ.
5. (Conclusion.) By 0(a) (B is open), 0(c) for μ_{R_Z} and steps 3, 4, 2: M_B(Z) = μ_{R_Z}(B) = μ_{R_Z}(W) + μ_{R_Z}(Σ) + μ_{R_Z}(O′) ≤ (M_W(S) + e) + e + b. With step 1, b has both required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: b := μ_T(B ∖ F). B = W ⊔ (F ∖ W) ⊔ (B ∖ F), μ_T(F ∖ W) = 0 and mass_and_support give M_B(T) = M_W(T) + b.
On B ∖ F both S − C and Ŷ vanish (vanish_off_support), so Z = T there and μ_Z(B ∖ F) ≤ b.
On W, currentEval(T, ιω) = T(ω) gives Z(ω) = S(ιω) − Sr(ιω), so μ_Z(W) = M_W(Z) ≤ M_W(S) + M(Sr) ≤ M_W(S) + e.
On F ∖ W, inside the open U′ = U ∖ spt(S − C), Z = T + Ŷ; compact_outer_bound with ν = μ_T + μ_Ŷ gives μ_Z(F ∖ W) ≤ 0 + μ_Ŷ(F ∖ W) ≤ e.
Add the three regional bounds: M_B(Z) = μ_Z(B) ≤ M_W(S) + e + e + b.

subproblems.title: Cancelling the finite mass outside F in [0, ∞] (parent step 8)
subproblems.statement: Let a, b, s, e, M ∈ [0, ∞], L ∈ ℝ and n ∈ ℕ, with 1 ≤ L, b ≤ M and M ≠ ∞. If a + b ≤ ofReal(Lⁿ)·(s + e + e + b), then a ≤ ofReal(Lⁿ)·(s + 2e) + ofReal(Lⁿ − 1)·M. Here ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal, and all arithmetic is in [0, ∞].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (a b s e M : ℝ≥0∞) (L : ℝ) (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ L → b ≤ M → M ≠ ∞ → a + b ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (L ^ n) * (s + e + e + b) → a ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (L ^ n) * (s + 2 * e) + ENNReal.ofReal (L ^ n - 1) * M
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 8 (“a + b ≤ λ(s + e + e + b) = λ(s + 2e) + λb. Since λ ≥ 1, λb = b + (λ − 1)b in [0, ∞], and b < ∞ can be cancelled: a ≤ λ(s + 2e) + (λ − 1)b ≤ λ(s + 2e) + (λ − 1)M_{B_{G₃}}(T). Finally λ − 1 = ofReal(Lⁿ) − ofReal(1) = ofReal(Lⁿ − 1)”), stated abstractly. No siblings are used.
1. b ≠ ∞, since b ≤ M and M ≠ ∞.
2. L ≥ 1 gives Lⁿ ≥ 1 (one_le_pow₀), so Lⁿ − 1 ≥ 0. Write Lⁿ = 1 + (Lⁿ − 1) with both summands ≥ 0. ENNReal.ofReal_add then gives λ := ofReal(Lⁿ) = ofReal(1) + ofReal(Lⁿ − 1) = 1 + κ, where κ := ofReal(Lⁿ − 1).
3. In the commutative semiring [0, ∞], s + e + e + b = (s + 2e) + b. Hence λ(s + e + e + b) = λ(s + 2e) + λb = λ(s + 2e) + (1 + κ)b = (λ(s + 2e) + κb) + b.
4. So the hypothesis reads a + b ≤ (λ(s + 2e) + κb) + b. As b ≠ ∞ (step 1), b can be cancelled on the right (ENNReal.le_of_add_le_add_right): a ≤ λ(s + 2e) + κb.
5. Since b ≤ M, and multiplication and addition are monotone in [0, ∞], κb ≤ κM. Hence a ≤ λ(s + 2e) + κM = ofReal(Lⁿ)·(s + 2e) + ofReal(Lⁿ − 1)·M. ∎
proof_key_steps: b ≤ M < ∞, and ofReal(Lⁿ) = 1 + ofReal(Lⁿ − 1) because Lⁿ ≥ 1.
The right side equals (ofReal(Lⁿ)(s + 2e) + ofReal(Lⁿ − 1)b) + b; cancel the finite b.
Replace b by M using b ≤ M.
